notes: Route: WP REST API https://www.rappler.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?after=2026-09-24T00:00:00&before=2026-10-26T23:59:59&per_page=100&page=N, site-local (PHT) 'date' field as the publication date. robots.txt (200) disallows only /wp-json/rappler/ and AI crawlers; /wp-json/wp/v2/ is allowed and returned 200 on every page (8 pages, 776 items, last page 76 < 100 = complete). Date choice: REST 'date' is PHT (UTC+8) and matches the site's own display exactly — the /latest/ listing pages carry <time datetime="...+08:00" title="Oct 26, 2026 ... PHT"> and article pages carry the same PHT instant; JSON-LD datePublished holds the same instant in UTC, so the PHT date is within 0-1 days of either reading (all 6 spot-checked samples: delta 0, ~500-800k chars text). Why not other routes: post-sitemap.xml (first of 419 sitemaps) holds 2001-2006 archive posts, not current articles; news-sitemap.xml has only ~11 newest URLs; /latest/page/N/ pagination shows only 10 articles/page (~300 requests for the window vs 8 for REST). Result: 736 unique URLs, all 31 days of the window present (min 10 on 2026-10-11; the three check days: 2026-09-30=24, 2026-10-10=17, 2026-10-20=25). Cross-checked 2026-10-20 against the site's own /latest/ feed: 23 items listed there, 25 in the TSV — same order of magnitude, dates agree. Runs in ~40s at polite_fetch rate 1-2 req/s.
